opener.dateline:
Ministry of Foreign Affairs,
Cairo, May 30, 1880.

div.p: Mr. Agent and Consul-General: The period of five years for which the tribunals of the reform were instituted will end the 31st of January next.
The Government of His Highness the Khedive, impressed with the idea of the service that this institution has rendered to Egypt, desires to assure its continuance during a new period of five years.

It is of the opinion, however, that the experience acquired has demonstrated the necessity of making certain modifications, as well in the règlement d’organisation judiciaire as in the provisions themselves, of the codes, and it desires that these modifications be studied and elaborated mutually by it and the powers that have accepted the reform.

The Government of His Hghness has therefore the honor, Mr. Agent and Consul-General, to beg you to be so kind as to ask of your government the necessary powers to take part in the labors of an international commission to assemble at Cairo under the presidency of his excellency the minister of justice.

Each member of the commission might be authorized by his government to procure the assistance of a delegate or assistant commissioner having a right of discussion but not voting. It will be lawful, moreover, for the commissioners to appoint a committee, whose composition and powers it will determine, to prepare in whole or in part the drafts of the modifications to be submitted to its deliberations.

I have no need, Mr. Agent and Consul-General, to ask you to advise your government of the importance of the commission in question commencing its work within a time that will permit its termination before the epoch at which the powers of the tribunals of the reform will expire.
Accept, Mr. Agent and Consul-General, the assurance of my high consideration.

closer.signed:
MUSTAPHA FEHMI,
Minister of Foreign Affairs.
